newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February jobless rate at 2.97 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February jobless rate at 2.97 percent.

text.p: Taiwan's unemployment rate was at 2.97 percent in February, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.

A directorate official said about 100,000 people would lose their jobs due to an emergency ban on exports from one of Taiwan's top export sectors, pork production, which is reeling from an island-wide outbreak of pig foot-and-mouth disease.
The agency said the jobless rate for all of 1997 would be about three percent, well above a government cabinet estimate of 2.6 percent, with the rise blamed chiefly on the pork crisis.
The cabinet's Council of Agriculture on March 20 slapped a temporary ban on all exports of fresh and frozen pork -- a US$3.24 billion a year industry employing 700,000 people.
At 2.97 percent, the jobless rate for February came in slightly above an average forecast of 2.81 percent compiled in a March 21 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

Economists interviewed in the Reuters Poll had said they expected February joblessness to remain at comparatively high levels due to the slow pace of new employment reflecting the economic recovery's relative slowness.

Taiwan's jobless rate held close to 1.5 percent in 1991-1994 but rose to 1.79 percent in 1995 and pushed above 3.0 percent in August, September and October 1996, but fellow below 3.0 percent in November and December.
The jobless rate was 2.60 percent for all of 1996.
January's jobless rate was just 2.68 percent, raising hopes that the recovery was picking up steam.

Officials had attributed the shift to higher jobless levels to a fundamental change in Taiwan's economy -- a broad move toward service-oriented industries from labour-intensive manufacturing that had engendered the island's dramatic economic development.
The number of unemployed people in February increased 26,000 to 278,000 from January. The number of employed dropped 102,000 to 9.078 million.
